name: gold_for_the_portal
revision: r1 (2026-11-10): written from the parked pitch with the critic's fix applied (a piglin steps through wearing Grandpa's gold helmet; planted early)
caption: why does grandma feed the nether portal 😶
logline: Every night Grandma throws one gold ingot into the Nether portal in the cellar and every morning a gift comes back, so her grandson Milo is sure Grandpa is alive over there, until he throws in a whole stack to buy Grandpa's way home and a piglin steps out wearing Grandpa's helmet.
question: why tf does grandma throw gold into a nether portal every night?
premise: Grandpa went into the Nether 25 years ago wearing Grandma's gold helmet with the blue stripe ('gold keeps you safe in the Nether') and never came back. Every night since, Grandma throws one gold ingot into the portal in the cellar (9,000 of them), and every morning something comes back out of it: obsidian, string, ender pearls, fire resistance potions. Grandma says he's still trading. Milo keeps the gifts in a barrel and knows Grandpa is alive.
twist: The gifts are a piglin's barters: piglins take a gold ingot and throw back a random item from the barter list. Grandpa died over there long ago; a piglin picked his helmet up where he fell (piglins pick up and wear gold armour) and has traded with Grandma every night since, because she is the only one who feeds it gold. Grandma has known for years ('Just one, Milo. One's plenty.'). Tonight Milo throws in a whole stack to buy Grandpa's way home, the piglin comes through after the gold, and it is wearing Grandpa's helmet. Shaking (a piglin in the Overworld starts to zombify), it turns after the ingot Grandma tosses back into the purple: she sends it home.

lines.text: My grandma has thrown / NINE THOUSAND / gold ingots / into a PORTAL.
lines.direction: one quick bright breath, amazed and proud of her; the number lands hardest

lines.text: One every NIGHT. / And every MORNING, / something comes BACK.
lines.direction: a storyteller's grin; a small beat before the last two words

lines.text: OBSIDIAN. / STRING. / ENDER PEARLS. / A potion that makes you FIREPROOF.
lines.direction: a quick excited list, each item a little bigger; the last one is the best present in the world

lines.text: Twenty-five years ago, / Grandma gave Grandpa / her gold HELMET. / With a BLUE stripe.
lines.direction: slower, proud, the family legend; lean on the colour

lines.text: Gold keeps you SAFE / in the NETHER, she said. / He went IN. / He never came BACK.
lines.direction: quoting her proudly, then the energy drops for the last sentence; a short stop before it
lines.say: Gold keeps you safe in the Nether, she said. He went in. <short pause> He never came back.

lines.text: I keep his gifts / in a BARREL. / Grandma says / he's still TRADING.
lines.direction: bright again, sure of it; the last word said like a fact everybody knows

lines.text: So he's ALIVE / over there. / I KNOW it.
lines.direction: full volume, certain, a little defiant, like someone said he wasn't
gentle and firm, a small smile; a beat after the name
lines.say: Just one, Milo. <short pause> One's plenty.

lines.text: When she went to BED, / I threw in / ALL my gold. / SIXTY-FOUR. / To buy his way HOME.
lines.direction: sneaky and fast, then huge hope on the last words

lines.text: Then I sat / and WAITED. / And something / stepped OUT.
lines.direction: slower, full volume, real nerves creeping in; a held beat before the last two words
lines.say: Then I sat and waited. <short pause> And something stepped out.

lines.direction: full volume, slow, the wonder cracking into understanding on the last word; no tears, just a kid seeing it
